{{nihongo|'''Nagato Uzumaki'''|渦巻長門|lead=yes}}, known primarily under the alias of {{nihongo|'''Pain'''| ペイン |Pein|lead=yes}}, is a fictional character in the [[manga]] and [[anime]] series ''[[Naruto]]'' created by [[Masashi Kishimoto]], and is a major [[antagonist]] in the series.

Nagato Uzumaki is the public figurehead leader of the [[List of Naruto characters#Akatsuki|Akatsuki]] who wishes to capture all the tailed beasts sealed into various people around the shinobi world. After acquiring and sealing most of the beasts within the Gedo statue, Nagato's advisor, [[Obito Uchiha]] who controlled the Akatsuki in reality, advises him to capture the Nine-Tailed Demon Fox named Kurama that was sealed inside the series' main [[protagonist]], [[Naruto Uzumaki]]. Before leaving to capture Naruto, Nagato engages in a mortal battle with his former mentor, [[Jiraiya (Naruto)|Jiraiya]]. His past as a war orphan, and his loss of his best friend Yahiko are explored. Due to his traumatic experiences, which stemmed from human conflict, Nagato aims to create a new world, free from the chaos of war. Nagato also appears in the series' [[video game]]s.

Nagato was conceived by Kishimoto as a villain, a victim of war, who would show Naruto the impact and gravity of world wars, something Kishimoto aimed to explore throughout the series. While Nagato does not fight in the story, he uses a group of corpses known as {{nihongo|"The Six Paths of Pain"|ペイン六道|Pein Rikudō}}. All of them were given elaborate designs with multiple piercings across their bodies to reinforce the idea that despite his calm demeanor, Nagato is a dangerous person.

Critical response to Nagato's character has been generally positive, praising the chaos he brings to the story, including the murder of Jiraiya and the destruction of the Hidden Leaf itself while chasing Naruto. His eventual fight against Naruto has been regarded as one of the best battles in the entire series.

==Creation and design==
[[File:SixPathsofPain.png|thumb|400px|left|The Six Paths of Pain as seen in the manga of ''Naruto''|alt=A group of six red-haired characters wearing black clothes who have multiple piercings]]
[[File:Rinnegan.svg|100px|thumb|Nagato's Rinnegan]]
Nagato originated from [[Masashi Kishimoto]]'s desire to elaborate on the ending to the [[manga]] series ''[[Naruto]]''. While the series was known for its fight scenes and tragedies, the main characters never experienced a war. Once the series began its "second part", simply referred to as Part II in the manga and ''Shippuden'' in the [[anime]], Kishimoto felt the need to create a story arc that would emphasize the tragedy of wars, leading to the final arc which would include a war. The principal reason for this was a significant difference between the two main characters, [[Naruto Uzumaki]] who had no knowledge of wars, and [[Sasuke Uchiha]] who was a victim of one; his entire clan had been annihilated to avoid a potential civil war. As a result, Kishimoto created Nagato as a war victim who would kill Naruto's teacher, [[Jiraiya (Naruto)|Jiraiya]], and act as Naruto's arch nemesis so he would understand the tragedy that Sasuke had experienced. This led to the creation of the series' final arc, the Fourth Great Shinobi War, where Naruto engages in a bigger fight with the remaining members of the terrorist organization [[List of Naruto characters#Akatsuki|Akatsuki]].<ref name="Koba">{{Cite AV media |script-title=ja:漫道コバヤシ第13号「Naruto完結！岸本斉史SP」 |date=December 13, 2014 |language=ja |publisher=[[Fuji Television]] |trans-title=Kobayashi No. 13 'Completion of Naruto! Masashi Kishimoto SP'}}</ref>

According to Kishimoto, Pain's story arc was the most difficult one to write. He felt this because the [[protagonist]], Naruto, truly forgave his enemy. Instead of having the protagonist kill the enemy he hates as happens in other series, Kishimoto found the idea of the two characters interacting and settling their differences more challenging.<ref name="comiconinter">{{cite web|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interview/2015-10-14/masashi-kishimoto-at-new-york-comic-con/.94186 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161019091230/http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interview/2015-10-14/masashi-kishimoto-at-new-york-comic-con/.94186 |archive-date=October 19, 2016 |title=Masashi Kishimoto at New York Comic-con The Anime News Network Interview |website=[[Anime News Network]] |author=Aoki, Deb |date=October 14, 2015 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> This had a major impact on the writer, and he decided to have Naruto forgive Sasuke during their final fight in a similar manner as he interacted with Nagato.<ref name="comiconinter"/> Retrospectively, Kishimoto believes ''Naruto'' took a darker tone with Nagato's introduction due to how his life indicated serious themes rarely present in ''[[shonen manga]]'' and thus often questioned himself what type of conclusion to this fight between the Akatsuki and the main character.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vix.com/es/btg/comics/4294/imperdible-doble-entrevista-a-masashi-kishimoto-tras-el-final-de-naruto|title=Imperdible doble entrevista a Masashi Kishimoto tras el final de Naruto|website=Vix|language=es|access-date=July 8, 2020}}</ref>

Regarding the bonds in the story, Kishimoto highlighted the importance of Jiraiya's death during his fight against Pain; this remark was made since, in his last moments, Jiraiya managed to discover the origin of Pain's multiple bodies and used his remaining forces to send a message to Naruto in which he explained how Pain can be defeated.<ref name=Kizuna>{{cite book|script-title=ja:Naruto－ナルト－名言集 絆－Kizuna－ 天ノ巻|publisher=[[Shueisha]]|year=2013|isbn=978-4-08-720681-4|author=Kishimoto, Masashi|pages=188–195|author-link=Masashi Kishimoto}}</ref> As Nagato was Akatsuki's leader, Kishimoto aimed to give him a striking design showing an appealing look while simultaneously depicting him as a dangerous person. Since his alias is "Pain", he decided to add some piercings to his body—a metaphor for how he inflicts "pain upon himself". Notable among the few unused concept designs for him is a small sketch where Pain appears to wear a partial mask with a feather or horn-like accessories fitted to his forehead protector.<ref name="data3889">{{cite book|author=Kishimoto, Masashi|title=Naruto Character Official Data Book Hiden Sha no Sho|year=2008|publisher=[[Shueisha]]|isbn=978-4-08-874247-2|pages=348–349|author-link=Masashi Kishimoto}}</ref>

In the Japanese anime, Nagato's voice actor is [[Junpei Morita]], while Yahiko/Deva(Literally meaning "God" in Hindi)/Tendo Path is voiced by [[Kenyu Horiuchi]]; in the English dub, Nagato is voiced by [[Vic Mignogna]], and Yahiko/Deva Path is voiced by [[Troy Baker]] (except for ''[[Naruto Shippuden: Ultimate Ninja Storm 4|Ultimate Ninja Storm 4]]'', where he is voiced by [[Matthew Mercer]]). While the other Paths shared the Deva Path's voice actors, the second Animal Path is voiced by Shiho Hisajima in Japanese and [[Stephanie Sheh]] in English.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/characters/Naruto/Nagato/|title=Nagato|access-date=July 7, 2019|publisher=Behind the Voice Actors|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190707232555/https://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/characters/Naruto/Nagato/|archive-date=July 7, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/characters/Naruto/Pain-Tendo/|title=Pain (Tendo)|access-date=July 7, 2019|publisher=Behind the Voice Actors|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190707232554/https://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/characters/Naruto/Pain-Tendo/|archive-date=July 7, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> In regard to Nagato, Mignogna said "his story arc is amazing".<ref>{{cite tweet |author=Vic Mignogna|user=vicmignogna |number = 260451182915502080 |date=October 22, 2012 |title=Time to record naruto!! NAGATO! His story arc is amazing!!|access-date=July 10, 2019}}</ref>

==Appearances==
Nagato is the recognized leader of the Akatsuki and [[List of Naruto characters#Konan|Konan]]'s partner, with [[Obito Uchiha]] acting as his benefactor.<ref name="Kishimoto, Masashi 2012">{{cite book|title=Naruto|volume=54|chapter=510|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|author=Kishimoto, Masashi|year=2012|isbn=978-1-4215-4102-0|author-link=Masashi Kishimoto|title-link=Naruto}}</ref> The "Pain" that is most often seen and used in the series is the Deva Path. This is actually Nagato's deceased friend {{nihongo|Yahiko|弥彦}}, one of six animated corpses collectively known as "The Six Paths of Pain" that are controlled by Nagato and use one sixth of his full power.<ref name="pain">{{cite book|title=Naruto|volume=41|chapter=378|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|author=Kishimoto, Masashi|year=2009|isbn=978-1-4215-2842-7|author-link=Masashi Kishimoto|title-link=Naruto}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Naruto|volume=45|chapter=419|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|author=Kishimoto, Masashi|year=2009|isbn=978-1-4215-3135-9|author-link=Masashi Kishimoto|title-link=Naruto}}</ref> The Pain Paths are all outfitted with a number of body piercings that serve as a means for Nagato to control them and offer them a "more dangerous" appearance in relation to their name's installation. Through Nagato's {{nihongo|Rinnegan|輪廻眼||{{lit|[[Saṃsāra]] Eye}}}}, they can share visual information and coordinate attacks.<ref name="pain"/>

Orphaned from the war-torn country of Amegakure, the Village Hidden in Rain, Nagato meets fellow orphans that he would become very close to named Konan and Yahiko, before they are all trained by Jiraiya. A descendant of the Uzumaki clan like Naruto, Nagato's Rinnegan is later revealed to have belonged to [[Madara Uchiha]], who transplanted his eyes into the child as part of his plan.<ref>{{cite book|title=Naruto|volume=41|chapter=510|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|author=Kishimoto, Masashi|year=2009|isbn=978-1-4215-4102-0|author-link=Masashi Kishimoto|title-link=Naruto}}</ref> Nagato desires peace for the world, helping Yahiko to create the Akatsuki to achieve that shared dream.<ref>{{cite book|title=Naruto|volume=54|chapter=373|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|author=Kishimoto, Masashi|year=2009|isbn=978-1-4215-2842-7|author-link=Masashi Kishimoto|title-link=Naruto}}</ref> The anime reveals Nagato is observed from afar by Madara's apprentice [[Obito Uchiha|Tobi]], who assumes Madara's identity. Following Yahiko's death, which Tobi orchestrated, by the actions of Hanzo of the Salamander, who was the Hidden Rain village leader, and [[Danzo Shimura]] of the Hidden Leaf Village, Nagato rethinks the idea that peace can only be attained by teaching the world suffering caused by war. For this, Nagato adopts the name of "Pain" and kills Hanzo, taking over as the new leader of the Hidden Rain and becoming a "[[God (male deity)|god]]" for its citizens. Crippled from both Hanzo's attack and his link with the Gedo Statue, Nagato finds a way to overcome his weakness by remotely controlling the corpses of deceased people as if they were their own. Besides Yahiko, Nagato creates the other Paths from the corpses of five ninja that Jiraiya encountered in the past. After this, unaware that Tobi is manipulating him, Pain begins leading the Akatsuki to force the world into peace using any means necessary.<ref>{{cite book|title=Naruto|volume=40|chapter=369|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|author=Kishimoto, Masashi|year=2009|isbn=978-1-4215-2841-0|author-link=Masashi Kishimoto|title-link=Naruto}}</ref>

Pain is confronted by his former mentor Jiraiya while infiltrating the Hidden Rain, resulting in a fight that ends with his mentor's death and the loss of his Animal Path vessel.<ref>{{cite book|title=Naruto|volume=42|chapter=383|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|author=Kishimoto, Masashi|year=2009|isbn=978-1-4215-2843-4|author-link=Masashi Kishimoto|title-link=Naruto}}</ref> Nagato converts the corpse of a Rain kunoichi named {{nihongo|Ajisai|アジサイ|Ajisai}} into a new Animal Path before beginning his attack on the Hidden Leaf. The rest of the Paths are destroyed in the fight against Naruto, with the Deva Path disabled,<ref>{{cite book|title=Naruto|volume=47|chapter=442|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|author=Kishimoto, Masashi|year=2010|isbn=978-1-4215-3305-6|author-link=Masashi Kishimoto|title-link=Naruto}}</ref> and Nagato recovers his faith in Jiraiya and world peace while talking with Naruto. He then sacrifices his life to revive the people he killed in the Hidden Leaf. Konan takes Nagato's and Yahiko's bodies to be placed in a tomb.<ref>{{cite book|title=Naruto|volume=47|chapter=448|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|author=Kishimoto, Masashi|year=2010|isbn=978-1-4215-3474-9|author-link=Masashi Kishimoto|title-link=Naruto}}</ref> Tobi desecrates Nagato's resting place to acquire the Rinnegan, which Madara later reclaims once fully resurrected.<ref name="Kishimoto, Masashi 2012"/> Nagato is reanimated by Tobi's ally [[Kabuto Yakushi]] during the war and sent alongside former ally [[Itachi Uchiha]] to battle Naruto and [[List of Naruto characters#Killer Bee|Killer Bee]]. Though he regains some of his ability to fight again, Nagato gets sealed by the combined efforts of Itachi, Killer Bee and Naruto and is sent back to the afterlife.<ref>{{cite book|title=Naruto|volume=58|chapter=551|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|author=Kishimoto, Masashi|year=2012|isbn=978-1-4215-4328-4|author-link=Masashi Kishimoto|title-link=Naruto}}</ref>

Besides the main series, Nagato appears in multiple [[video game]]s based on the series.<ref name="stormtwo">{{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/2010/10/16/9-questions-for-naruto-shippuden-ultimate-ninja-storm-2s-hiroshi-matsuyama/|title=9 Questions for Naruto Shippuden: Ultimate Ninja Storm 2's Hiroshi Matsuyama|date=October 16, 2010|publisher=[[VentureBeat]]|access-date=July 28, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161003033937/http://venturebeat.com/2010/10/16/9-questions-for-naruto-shippuden-ultimate-ninja-storm-2s-hiroshi-matsuyama/|archive-date=October 3, 2016|df=mdy-all}}</ref> The game ''[[Naruto Shippuden: Ultimate Ninja Storm Revolution]]'' shows the organization of the Akatsuki group.<ref name="ASidestory2">{{cite web|url=http://www.siliconera.com/2014/03/06/naruto-shippuden-ultimate-ninja-storm-revolution-50-minutes-new-anime/|title=Naruto Shippuden: Ultimate Ninja Storm Revolution Has Over 50 Mins. Of New Anime|publisher=Siliconera|date=March 6, 2014|access-date=March 11, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140311073743/http://www.siliconera.com/2014/03/06/naruto-shippuden-ultimate-ninja-storm-revolution-50-minutes-new-anime/|archive-date=March 11, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> Nagato's actions are also present in the [[light novel]] ''Akatsuki Hiden: Evil Flowers in Full Bloom'' as a story Sasuke Uchiha learns while wandering across the world.<ref>{{cite book|author=Kishimoto, Masashi|title=Akatsuki Hiden: Evil Flowers in Full Bloom|last2=Towada, Shin|publisher=[[Shueisha]]|year=2015|isbn=978-4-08-703367-0}}</ref>

==Reception==
Nagato has been a popular character from the ''Naruto'' series. ''[[IGN]]'' listed him as the fourth best character in the story. The site called him "one of the most philosophically and psychologically complex characters" due to the depth he brought to the series and the impact he had on the story, not only for his crimes but for the way he tried to redeem himself in his final moments interacting with Naruto.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/top-10-naruto-characters?page=2|title=Top 10 Naruto Characters|author=Isler, Ramsey|date=November 12, 2014|publisher=[[IGN]]|access-date=July 7, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190426160900/https://www.ign.com/articles/top-10-naruto-characters?page=2|archive-date=April 26, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> IGN felt Nagato's battle with Jiraiya was the franchise's second best fight, adding it might be one of the best animated fights in anime history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://es.ign.com/naruto-1/86392/feature/los-20-mejores-duelos-de-naruto-y-naruto-shippuden?p=4|title=Los 20 mejores duelos de Naruto y Naruto Shippuden|publisher=[[IGN]]|access-date=July 7, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180407170501/http://es.ign.com/naruto-1/86392/feature/los-20-mejores-duelos-de-naruto-y-naruto-shippuden?p=4|archive-date=April 7, 2018|url-status=live|date=November 10, 2014}}</ref> On the other hand, ''[[Anime News Network]]'' criticized the story of Nagato and Jiraiya, feeling that Sasuke Uchiha's conflict with the Akatsuki was far more entertaining; nevertheless, the fact that Nagato killed his former teacher was said to have a major impact on the series.<ref name="manga">{{cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/house-of-1000-manga/2014-11-13/naruto-part-ii/.80991|title=House of 1000 Manga Naruto Part II|access-date=July 7, 2019|publisher=[[Anime News Network]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190426161146/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/house-of-1000-manga/2014-11-13/naruto-part-ii/.80991|archive-date=April 26, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> In a manga popularity poll, Nagato was voted the 23rd most popular ''Naruto'' character.<ref>{{cite book |last=Kishimoto|first=Masashi|author-link=Masashi Kishimoto|title=Naruto, Volume 56|year=2011 |publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 519|isbn=978-4088702186}}</ref>

Critical response to Nagato's role in the series has been positive. ''Anime UK News'' praised his invasion of Konohagakure, mainly due to the chaos he created during the fights, offering the audience a sensation of hopelessness as multiple characters were defeated and killed, yet still providing hope that Naruto would be able to defeat Nagato due to his constant training. The reviewer also felt the appearance of [[Konohamaru Sarutobi]], a younger ninja friend of Naruto, to defeat one of the six Pains was appealing but said the anime's production did not live up to the original manga.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://animeuknews.net/2013/08/naruto-shippuuden-volume-13/|title=Naruto: Shippuuden Volume 13|publisher=Anime UK News|access-date=July 7, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190426222901/https://animeuknews.net/2013/08/naruto-shippuuden-volume-13/|archive-date=April 26, 2019|url-status=live|date=August 18, 2013}}</ref> ''Anime News Network'' said the major destruction Nagato brought to the village had a great impact, most notably when the area became empty because of one of his techniques.<ref name="manga"/> His eventual fight against Naruto has been praised for the fact that both fighters used interesting tactics during the battle, with ''Mania Entertainment'' sensing a major change in Naruto as he was haunted by the idea of avenging Jiraiya.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mania.com/naruto-shippuden-episode-164_article_123143.html|title=Naruto: Shippuuden Episode 164|archive-date=November 30, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121130104933/http://www.mania.com/naruto-shippuden-episode-164_article_123143.html}}</ref> ''The Fandom Post'' wrote that Nagato impacted both the story and Naruto when he nearly killed [[Hinata Hyuga]] once Naruto was overwhelmed by him. The new motivation Naruto had for defeating the Akatsuki was praised despite the mixed responses to the way he defeated Nagato in the next episodes.<ref name="fandomuk"/> ''UK Anime Network'' also praised Nagato's actions during the invasion and the fights for all the damage he caused to the village. The reviewer recommended these scenes to newcomers because of how interesting the story had become and felt this arc was the best part of the series for fans. However, the reviewer strongly criticized the animation Studio Pierrot produced for an episode where the struggle between Nagato and Naruto continued.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uk-anime.net/anime/Naruto_Shippuden_Box_Set_14.html|title=Naruto Shippuden Box Set 14|access-date=July 7, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180427001014/http://www.uk-anime.net/Anime/Naruto_Shippuden_Box_Set_14.html|archive-date=April 27, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> In contrast to ''UK Anime Network'', another reviewer for ''The Fandom Post'' thought the anime adaptation managed to make the fight between Nagato and Naruto entertaining in terms of movements, audio and voice acting. They felt Nagato's words regarding his philosophy of war had a big impact on Naruto, who said he cannot fight back.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fandompost.com/2013/05/17/naruto-shippuden-dvd-set-14-anime-dvd-review/|title=Naruto: Shippuden DVD Set 14 Anime DVD Review|date=May 17, 2013 |access-date=July 7, 2019|publisher=The Fandom Post}}</ref> ''Anime News Network'' felt that the entire battle managed to be one of the best in the series because of the tactics used by the two characters, and had a notable emotional impact on viewers.<ref name="ann"/>

Following the battle that ended when Naruto defeated all six Pains after which Nagato interacted with him. Nagato's past was viewed as too tragic by ''Anime News Network'', citing the death of his parents among other desperate scenes that led the reviewer to feel it was too dark for a series aimed at a young demographic.<ref name="ann">{{cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/naruto-shippuden/dvd-set-14|title=Naruto Shippūden DVD Set 14|access-date=July 7, 2019|publisher=Anime News Network|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190526065446/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/naruto-shippuden/dvd-set-14|archive-date=May 26, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> ''The Fandom Post'' felt that Naruto's intention to follow Jiraiya's wish for world peace against Nagato's philosophy of a world of chaos had a major impact on the story. The way Naruto presented his ideals to Nagato brought further depth to the series.<ref name="fandomuk">{{cite web|url=https://www.fandompost.com/2013/10/10/naruto-shippuden-dvd-set-14-uk-anime-dvd-review/|title=Naruto: Shippuden DVD Set 14 The Fandom Post|access-date=July 7, 2019|publisher=The Fandom Post|date=October 10, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190426161748/https://www.fandompost.com/2013/10/10/naruto-shippuden-dvd-set-14-uk-anime-dvd-review/|archive-date=April 26, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> However, Nagato's final actions, including killing himself to revive some of the people he murdered, got a mixed responses from ''Anime News Network'' because it reduced the tension and drama he had built in the story.<ref name="fandomuk"/><ref name="manga"/>

Tail]], Volume 54|year=2016|publisher=[[Kodansha]]|chapter=Chapter 464|isbn=978-4-06-395626-9|author-link=Hiro Mashima}} ==Reception== ===Critical response=== Critical reception of Natsu's character has generally been positive. Journalists have analyzed his characterization in the manga. While reviewing the manga series, Carl Kimlinger of ''[[Anime News Network]]'' (''ANN'') mentioned that the story usually followed the pattern where Natsu showed how strong he was every time he ended up in a bad situation. He also commented that Natsu has "strong principles, insane power", and a "wacky weakness", stating that all of these traits make him a model for characters from [[Shōnen manga|''shōnen'']] action manga.{{cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/fairy-tail/gn-1|title=Fairy Tail GN 1|date=May 28, 2008|last=Kimlinger|first=Carl|website=[[Anime News Network]]|access-date=February 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180324190151/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/fairy-tail/gn-1|archive-date=March 24, 2018|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}} Kimlinger said that placing Natsu against dangerous villains managed to create real interest. He further characterized Natsu as "an often frightening force", but he also depicted him as being "little more than a short fuse" with a sense of [[humor]] and motion sickness.{{cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/fairy-tail/gn-2|title=Fairy Tail GN 2|date=September 7, 2008|last=Kimlinger|first=Carl|website=[[Anime News Network]]|access-date=February 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180325013300/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/fairy-tail/gn-2|archive-date=March 25, 2018|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}} Carlo Santos of the same website thought that Natsu's fight against wind wizard Erigor, the acting leader of the dark guild Eisenwald, was the highlight of that particular volume. Santos further stated that Natsu being called a "flaming brat" added humor to the story.{{cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/fairy-tail/gn-3|title=Fairy Tail GN 3|date=July 20, 2008|last=Santos|first=Carlo|website=[[Anime News Network]]|access-date=February 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180325013657/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/fairy-tail/gn-3|archive-date=March 25, 2018|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}} He also commented that Natsu had become a hero following the events from the [[Tower of Heaven (Fairy Tail)|Tower of Heaven]]. The writer described Natsu's [[Battle cry|battle cries]] as "fierce" and his "flamethrowing magic" as "intense".{{cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/fairy-tail/gn-12|title=Fairy Tail GN 12|date=October 2, 2010|last=Santos|first=Carlo|website=[[Anime News Network]]|access-date=February 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180325014115/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/fairy-tail/gn-12|archive-date=March 25, 2018|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}} Rebecca Silverman of the same website wrote that Natsu proved to be both intelligent and creative during his fight with a villain from the Grimoire Heart guild.{{cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/fairy-tail/gn-27|title=Fairy Tail GN 27|date=October 27, 2013|last=Silverman|first=Rebecca|website=[[Anime News Network]]|access-date=February 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180325014456/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/fairy-tail/gn-27|archive-date=March 25, 2018|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}} Silverman further added that Natsu had started being depicted as falling suggestively on Lucy more often, and she believed this highlighted the idea of love and romance in the manga.{{cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/fairy-tail/gn-53/.101879|title=Fairy Tail GN 53|date=May 8, 2016|last=Silverman|first=Rebecca|website=[[Anime News Network]]|access-date=February 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180325015131/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/fairy-tail/gn-53/.101879|archive-date=March 25, 2018|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}} A. E. Sparrow of ''[[IGN]]'' mentioned that Natsu, being a fire wizard with motion sickness, is "a complex character", and he said that it would be fun to watch him throughout the series.{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2008/05/27/fairy-tail-vol-1-and-2-review|title=Fairy Tail: Vol. 1 and 2 Review|date=May 27, 2008|last=Sparrow|first=A. E.|website=[[IGN]]|access-date=February 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180325015535/http://www.ign.com/articles/2008/05/27/fairy-tail-vol-1-and-2-review|archive-date=March 25, 2018|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}} David West of ''[[Neo (magazine)|Neo]]'' felt that Natsu's fire-based abilities match his quick-tempered nature and said the character has a tendency to scuffle. The writer described Natsu as "reckless and wild", stating that the character's fire magic is destructive.{{cite web|url=http://www.neomag.co.uk/art/anime-manga/article/759/meet-the-dragon-king|title=Meet the Dragon King|magazine=[[Neo (magazine)|Neo]]|last=West|first=David|date=March 1, 2012|access-date=February 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180325020012/http://www.neomag.co.uk/art/anime-manga/article/759/meet-the-dragon-king|archive-date=March 25, 2018|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}} Dale North of ''Japanator'' regarded Natsu as "one of the best and most powerful" Fairy Tail members and described his fighting skills as "incredible".{{cite web|url=https://www.japanator.com/japanator-review-fairy-tail-vol-1-and-2-manga--7673.phtml|title=Japanator Review: Fairy Tail Vol. 1 and 2 (manga)|date=April 2, 2008|last=North|first=Dale|website=Japanator|access-date=April 27, 2018|archive-date=April 27, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180427220201/https://www.japanator.com/japanator-review-fairy-tail-vol-1-and-2-manga--7673.phtml|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}} Critics have also provided comments in regard to Natsu based on how he was depicted in ''Fairy Tail''{{'}}s animated adaptation and feature films. Vegeta Jr. (descendant; ''[[Dragon Ball GT]]'') | occupation = Inventor, engineer, and CEO of Capsule Corporation | species = Human | gender = Female }} {{nihongo|'''Bulma'''|ブルマ|Buruma|lead=yes}} is a fictional character in the ''[[Dragon Ball]]'' franchise, first appearing in the original [[manga]] series created by [[Akira Toriyama]], [[Goku]]'s first friend and the eventual wife of [[Vegeta]] and mother of [[Trunks (Dragon Ball)|Trunks]] and [[List of Dragon Ball characters#Bulla|Bulla]]. She made her appearance in the first chapter "Bulma and Son Goku", published in ''[[Weekly Shōnen Jump]]'' magazine on 19 June 1984, issue 51,{{cite web |url=http://mediaarts-db.jp/mg/magazines/322516 |script-title=ja:週刊少年ジャンプ 1984/06/19 表示号数51 |website=Media Arts Database |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |language=ja |access-date=21 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161009171854/http://mediaarts-db.jp/mg/magazines/322516 |archive-date=9 October 2016 |url-status=dead }} meeting [[Goku]] and befriending him and traveling together to find the wish-granting Dragon Balls. Bulma is the daughter of [[Dr. Brief]], the founder of Capsule Corporation, a company that creates special small capsules that shrink and hold objects of various sizes for easy storage. Being the daughter of a brilliant scientist, Bulma is also a scientific genius, as well as an inventor and engineer. Along with creating the [[Dragon Ball|Dragon Radar]], a device that detects the energy signal emitted by a Dragon Ball, Bulma's role as an inventor becomes important at several points in the series; including the [[Time travel|time machine]] that brings her future son [[Trunks (Dragon Ball)|Trunks]] to the past. ==Creation and design== [[File:A Modern Journey to the West7.jpg|thumb|upright|left|The relationship between Bulma and Goku is analogous to Wu Cheng'en's depiction of the dynamic between [[Sun Wukong]] and [[Tang Sanzang]].]] Bulma is loosely based on the character [[Tang Sanzang]] from the Chinese classic novel ''[[Journey to the West]]''.{{cite book |last=Toriyama|first=Akira|author-link1= Akira Toriyama|title= DRAGON BALL 大事典: STORY GUIDE|date= 9 August 1995|publisher= [[Shueisha]]|isbn=4-08-782752-6|language=ja|pages= 261–264|chapter= Akira Toriyama Super Interview: 2nd Round}} Bulma and Goku were the first pair of characters which were introduced in the manga and Toriyama stated that he subsequently introduced other characters in pairs because "that way, I'm able to explain the characters and their relationship to each other through their interactions. In my case, I feel that it isn't good to insert too much narration. I suppose Goku and Bulma are representative of that." He further added that "as a child, Goku doesn't know anything [of the world], so without Bulma, he'd be a character who didn't say anything."{{cite journal |title=Akira Toriyama Special Interview |journal=[[V Jump]] |publisher=[[Shueisha]] |date=21 May 2013}} The author also claimed that when the series started, his editor at the time, [[Kazuhiko Torishima]], wanted Bulma and Goku to form a romantic relationship.{{cite book |last=Toriyama |first=Akira |title=[[Dr. Slump]] |volume=16 |year=2008 |orig-year=1984 |publisher=[[Viz Media]] |isbn=978-1-4215-1060-6 |pages=[https://archive.org/details/drslumpvol160000tori/page/130 130] }} Bulma's appearance in the series is not as consistent as the other characters as she often changes her hairstyle and clothing, being fashion-conscious. Her hair is usually depicted in a shade of fuchsia, although in the first chapter and the anime, her hair is turquoise. When asked about the first time Bulma's hairstyle changed, Toriyama said it was to show that three years had passed and because he personally liked girls with short hair.{{cite journal |script-title=ja:ドラゴンボール 冒険SPECIAL |journal=[[Weekly Shōnen Jump]] |language =ja |publisher=[[Shueisha]] |pages=138–140 |date=1 December 1987}} She sometimes wears clothing with either her name on it or the Capsule Corporation logo. Her name "Buruma" is the Japanese pronunciation of "[[bloomers|bloomer]]", a type of gym shorts worn by Japanese girls at school.{{cite book|last1=Ledoux|first1=Trish|last2=Ranney|first2=Doug|editor-last1=Patten|editor-first1=Fred|title=The Complete Anime Guide: Japanese Animation Film Directory & Resource Guide|year=1997|publisher=Tiger Mountain Press|isbn=9780964954250|page=37|edition=2nd}}{{cite book|last=Levi|first=Antonia|title=Samurai From Outer Space: Understanding Japanese Animation|year=1996|publisher=Open Court|isbn=9780812693324|page=[https://archive.org/details/samuraifromouter00levi/page/60 60]|edition=1. print.|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/samuraifromouter00levi/page/60}}{{cite news|last = Smith|first = David|title = Knock 'Em Dead, Goku|publisher = [[IGN]]|date = 8 February 2008|url = http://www.ign.com/articles/2008/02/09/knock-em-dead-goku?page=2|archive-date = 23 February 2014|access-date = 20 July 2013|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140223223124/http://www.ign.com/articles/2008/02/09/knock-em-dead-goku?page=2|url-status = live}} As with most characters in the ''Dragon Ball'' series, Bulma's name is consistent with those of the rest of her family. All of Bulma's family members are named after underclothing of some sort. Her father's name is Dr. Brief, while her son and daughter are named Trunks and {{nihongo|Bra|ブラ|Bura|"Bulla" in the English anime dub}} respectively. Her mother is never named in the original series, being referred to only as {{nihongo|"Bulma's Mother"|ブルマのママ|Buruma no Mama}}. However, when asked in 2004 what name he would choose if he were to name her mother, Toriyama suggested {{nihongo|Panchy|パンチー|Panchī}}, a pun on [[panties]].{{cite book |last=Toriyama |first=Akira |title=Dragon Ball Forever |language=ja |year=2004 |publisher=[[Shueisha]] |pages=158–159 |isbn=4-08-873702-4}} However, in the video game, ''[[Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot]]'', Bulma's mother's name was revealed as {{nihongo|Bikini|ビキニ|Bikini}}. Toriyama stated in an interview that Bulma's family has a "[[laissez-faire]] attitude, but Bulma has complete control over things."{{cite book|title=DRAGON BALL 超全集 1: STORY & WORLD GUIDE|year=2013|publisher=[[Shueisha]]|isbn=978-4-08-782496-4|language=ja|pages=28–31|last=Toriyama|first=Akira}} ===Voice actors=== Bulma was voiced by [[Hiromi Tsuru]] in all Japanese media until her death in November 2017.{{cite news |url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO23597260X11C17A1CC0000/ |script-title=ja:声優の鶴ひろみさん死去 「アンパンマン」ドキンちゃん役 |last= |newspaper=[[The Nikkei]] |date=17 November 2017 |access-date=4 April 2025 |archive-date=4 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250404054142/https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO23597260X11C17A1CC0000/ |url-status=live}} As a new voice actress at the time, she had to audition for the part. She also said that all her previous roles were well-behaved characters, but Bulma was easy to play because she is down-to-earth.{{cite book|title=DRAGON BALL 大全集 補巻 TV ANIMATION PART 3|year=1996|publisher=[[Shueisha]]|pages=107–113|isbn=4-08-102019-1}} In February 2018, [[Aya Hisakawa]] was announced as the new voice actress for Bulma. In [[Funimation]]'s in house English dub, Bulma is voiced by [[Tiffany Vollmer]] in the original ''[[Dragon Ball (anime)|Dragon Ball]]'' series''.''{{Cite news|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/dragon-ball-z-kai/part-1|title=Dragon Ball Z Kai Part 1 Blu-Ray|work=Anime News Network|access-date=14 July 2017|language=en}} After Vollmer retired from voice acting, she was replaced by [[Monica Rial]] starting from ''[[Dragon Ball Z Kai]]''.{{Cite news|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2016-12-07/dragon-ball-z-kai-buu-saga-to-air-on-toonami/.109619|title=Dragon Ball Z Kai's Buu Saga to Air on Toonami|work=Anime News Network|access-date=14 July 2017|language=en|archive-date=28 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170728150244/http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2016-12-07/dragon-ball-z-kai-buu-saga-to-air-on-toonami/.109619|url-status=live}} === Characterization === Bulma's appearance in the anime is slightly different from the manga. In the manga version, her hair color is violet, while in the anime it is turquoise. Her long hairstyle stays shoulder-length as a teenager. She changes her hairstyle and cuts very often, and rarely wears the same dress for long periods. Many of the dresses that she wears bear her name or the Capsule Corporation logo. Bulma is presented as an extraordinarily intelligent individual, being able to create technology capable of feats beyond contemporary science. She usually displays strong analytical skills and the ability to recognize design and engineering styles. Although not a martial artist, Bulma occasionally defends herself with the use of firearms and other technological equipment. Like Goku, Bulma does not display the conventional heroic traits of helping others; Her selfishness is highlighted in her wishes with the Dragon Balls and her decision to leave Goku behind from a collapsing sea cave. In contrast, the Bulma of Future Trunks' dimension is characterised as selfless, shown by her decision to sacrifice herself to save Trunks from Goku Black. Bulma is also characterised as being courageous and straightforward, often choosing to accompany Goku into dangerous situations and criticising people for their wrongdoings. ==Appearances== ===''Dragon Ball''=== [[File:Bulma.jpg|thumb|upright|A teenaged Bulma as depicted in the character's first appearance.]] Bulma is introduced as the teenage inventor of the {{nihongo|Dragon Radar|ドラゴンレーダー|Doragon Rēdā}}, a device used to detect the Dragon Balls that she is searching for.{{cite book|last=Hollinger|first=Elizabeth M.|title=Dragonball Z: The legacy of Goku: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|year=2002|publisher=Prima Games|location=Roseville, CA|isbn=9780761539940|page=8}} She was hoping to use the Dragon Balls to wish for the perfect boyfriend. While searching for a nearby Dragon Ball, she runs into Goku and finds out that he inherited the four-star Dragon Ball from his adoptive father [[List of Dragon Ball characters#Grandpa Gohan|Grandpa Son Gohan]]. Because of Goku's love for the ball and his belief that his Grandpa's spirit lives in the ball, Goku is not willing to give it up. Bulma then asks him to loan it to her in exchange for taking him on her travels. At that point, they team up to find the remainder of the balls and the adventure begins.''Dragon Ball'' manga, volume 1 As the search progresses, Bulma and Goku meet [[Master Roshi]] after finding his pet turtle; [[List of Dragon Ball characters#Oolong|Oolong]], a shapeshifting pig who is terrorizing a village; and [[Yamcha]], and his shapeshifting cat companion [[Pu'ar]], a desert [[bandit]] who Bulma soon finds herself attracted to, and who she eventually starts a romantic relationship with. === ''Dragon Ball Z'' === After five years of peace, an evil menace comes to the Earth. It is Goku's elder brother, an extraterrestrial Saiyan named [[List of Dragon Ball characters#Raditz|Raditz]]. After Goku and [[Piccolo (Dragon Ball)|Piccolo]] kill him, Bulma takes the {{nihongo|Scouter|スカウター|Sukautā}} from Raditz and fixes it to find the power levels of people in human numbers. During the subsequent battle against Vegeta and [[List of Dragon Ball characters#Nappa|Nappa]], Yamcha, [[Tien Shinhan]], [[List of Dragon Ball characters#Chiaotzu|Chiaotzu]] and Piccolo are killed, and because Piccolo dies, the Dragon Balls are rendered useless.''Dragon Ball Z'' manga, volume 3 After Goku defeats the Saiyans, Bulma volunteers to travel to Piccolo's home planet, Namek, and use the Namekian Dragon Balls to restore Yamcha and the others back to life. In need of a spaceship, [[List of Dragon Ball characters#Mr. Popo|Mr. Popo]] reveals one to Bulma, which had been the ship [[Kami (Dragon Ball)|Kami]] had used to travel to Earth when he was a boy. She repairs the ship with the help of her father and flies off to Namek with [[Krillin]] and [[Son Gohan]].''Dragon Ball Z'' manga, volume 5 After Goku defeats the tyrant [[Frieza]], Yamcha and the others who were killed are revived by Porunga, the dragon of the Namekian Dragon Balls. Vegeta returns to Earth, staying with Bulma and her family. Several years before the arrival of the Androids, Bulma ends her relationship with Yamcha and begins a relationship with Vegeta that leads to the birth of their son, [[Trunks (Dragon Ball)|Trunks]].''Dragon Ball Z'' manga, volume 12 She used [[Dr. Gero]]'s stolen blueprints to build a detonator to destroy the Androids, but Krillin broke it after realizing his feelings for [[Android 18]]. With her father's help, Bulma later repairs [[List of Dragon Ball characters#Android 16|Android 16]] before the Tournament of Martial Arts. In the alternate future timeline, Bulma survives the Androids' onslaught and lives at the former site of Capsule Corp. She spends most of her life devoted to building a time machine, attempting to prevent the devastation brought by the Androids. She is very protective of Trunks and hates the idea of him fighting, but nevertheless allows him to travel to the past to deliver Goku an antidote for a heart virus that claimed his life in the alternate timeline. Once the Androids (or more importantly, [[Cell (Dragon Ball)|Cell]]) are taken care of in the main timeline, Trunks returns to his original time and defeats the much weaker Androids and Cell with ease, thus restoring peace to the future timeline world.''Dragon Ball Z'' manga, volume 19 Seven years after the battle against the Androids, Bulma helps Gohan by making a watch which automatically changes his clothes into a superhero costume so he could fight crime, without his real identity being known.''Dragon Ball Z'' manga, volume 20 She and the other heroes, except for Goku, Vegeta, Tien, Chiaotzu, and Gohan, hide at Kami's from the monstrous [[Majin Buu]], however, she is killed when Buu turns her into chocolate and eats her. Bulma is revived by the Porunga, along with the rest of the Earth, and gives her energy to Goku to eliminate Majin Buu once and for all.''Dragon Ball Z'' manga, volume 26 Many years later, she gives birth to her and Vegeta's daughter, [[List of Dragon Ball characters#Bra|Bulla]]. === ''Dragon Ball Super'' === Before Bulla's birth, during the events of ''[[Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods]]'' and the first half of the first season of ''Dragon Ball Super'', Bulma hosts a party with the prize being the Dragon Balls and unknowingly provoked the Destroyer God Beerus into nearly destroying Earth when she slapped him for ruining the event.''Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods'' She would soon learn of the resurrected Frieza's advance on Earth from her old friend {{nihongo|Jaco|ティリメンテンピボッシ • ジャコ|Tirimentenpibosshi Jako}} during the second half of the first season and ''[[Dragon Ball Z: Resurrection 'F']]'', narrowly escapes being when Frieza destroys Earth thanks to [[Whis]] rewinding the event so he can quickly be killed.''Dragon Ball Z: Resurrection 'F'' After Frieza's defeat, she creates the Super Dragon Radar to find the Super Dragon Balls in Universe 7 first to prevent Beerus from using them to wish for the total annihilation of the entire universe.''Dragon Ball Super'' anime, episode 29 The alternate timeline version of Bulma is killed by [[Goku Black]]. After Bulma reunites with Trunks,''Dragon Ball Super'' anime, episode 47 Bulma works on a time machine to send him back to his timeline to defeat Goku Black. After an unsuccessful attempt, Bulma travels with them to the timeline, showing Trunks a recording of Piccolo performing the ''Evil Containment Wave'' and fighting with and being injured by [[Zamasu]].{{cite episode|title=Praise and Adore Him! The Explosive Birth of Merged Zamasu!!|date=30 October 2016|series=Dragon Ball Super|number=64}} Bulma tries creating a time machine, only for Beerus to destroy it{{cite episode|title=Come Forth, Shenlong! Whose Wish Shall Be Granted?!|series=Dragon Ball Super|number=68|date=27 November 2016}} and she later summons Beerus to quell a perceived threat from [[Arale]] and then satisfies his taste by using Senbei's Reality Machine and viewers of the award ceremony she was attending to imagine the most tasteful food they could think of.{{cite episode|title=Goku vs Arale! Earth Ends in a Wacky Battle?!|number=69|series=Dragon Ball Super|date=4 December 2016}} In the Universe Survival Saga, Bulma agreed to pay 100 million Zeni to every member of Team Universe 7 who participated in the Tournament of Power if their team wins. It is also revealed that Bulla's birth is the result of Whis using his divine powers to hasten her conception, allowing Vegeta to participate in the tournament without worry.{{cite episode|title=Form the Seventh Universe Representative Team! Who Are the Strongest 10?!|number=83|series=Dragon Ball Super|date=26 March 2017}} She later accompanies Goku and Vegeta during the events of ''[[Dragon Ball Super: Broly]]'' when Frieza is trying to use Earth's Dragon Balls, revealed to have been using the wishes as a form of [[cosmetic surgery]] to maintain her youthful appearance. Following the event, as revealed in ''[[Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero]]'', Bulma established a branch of Capsule Corp to acquire the Dragon Balls for her so they would not fall into evil hands. === In Toriyama's films === Bulma appears in eight ''Dragon Ball Z'' films; in the [[Dragon Ball Z: Dead Zone|first movie]], Bulma makes a brief appearance when using the Dragon Radar to find Gohan after his abduction by Garlic Jr.'s henchman;''Dragon Ball Z: Dead Zone'' in the [[Dragon Ball Z: The World's Strongest|second]], she is used as leverage by Kochin to get Master Roshi to come back to the lair of Dr. Wheelo, where she is forced to accompany him as well;''Dragon Ball Z: The World's Strongest'' in the [[Dragon Ball Z: The Tree of Might|third]], she is seen camping with Oolong and Krillin before the Tree of Might is planted and later appears at Goku's home;''Dragon Ball Z: The Tree of Might'' in the [[Dragon Ball Z: Lord Slug|fourth]], Bulma's mind is probed by Lord Slug to aid in his quest to secure the Dragon Balls, her losing consciousness thereafter;''Dragon Ball Z: Lord Slug'' in the [[Dragon Ball Z: Broly - The Legendary Super Saiyan|eighth]], she makes a small appearance at the beginning, attending a picnic with the other characters;''Dragon Ball Z: Broly – The Legendary Super Saiyan'' in the [[Dragon Ball Z: Bojack Unbound|ninth]], Bulma watches a fighting tournament with Chi-Chi and Trunks while baring her [[midriff]] in a yellow tank [[crop top]] with short-shorts, a yellow [[headband]], and a pearl necklace; arguing with Chi-Chi during the shared viewing;''Dragon Ball Z: Bojack Unbound'' in the [[Dragon Ball Z: Fusion Reborn|twelfth]], Bulma gathers the Dragon Balls to send the souls of the deceased back to Other World;''Dragon Ball Z: Fusion Reborn'' in the [[Dragon Ball Z: Wrath of the Dragon|thirteenth]], Bulma creates a room for Tapion who she confronts over the friendship he has established with her son.''Dragon Ball Z: Wrath of the Dragon'' ===In other media=== Before the debut of the ''Dragon Ball'' anime, Bulma made her first anime debut in the film, ''[[Urusei Yatsura (film series)#Remember My Love|Remember My Love]]'' in the ''[[Urusei Yatsura]]'' series, released on 26 January 1985, albeit in a cameo role.{{cite web | url=https://comicbook.com/anime/news/dragon-ball-anime-bulma-first-appearance-urusei-yatsura/ | title=Dragon Ball Wasn't Actually the First Anime to Feature Bulma | date=11 February 2021 | access-date=22 March 2023 | archive-date=22 March 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230322185259/https://comicbook.com/anime/amp/news/dragon-ball-anime-bulma-first-appearance-urusei-yatsura/ | url-status=live }} In filler episodes of ''Dragon Ball Z'', during the Namek arc, Bulma travels to a fake Namek. While on Namek, she meets Captain Ginyu after his defeat by Goku, which results in him switching bodies with a frog. Because she does not know the frog's true identity, she bonds with him, leading her to create a machine for him to communicate with her. Ginyu uses the machine to utter the name of his technique ''Body Change'', allowing him to switch bodies with Bulma and leave her trapped in the frog's body. Bulma manages to stay around him as he looks for Frieza, and the two encounter Gohan, Krillin, and Piccolo while they are watching Goku and Frieza fight. Gohan realizes the change just as Ginyu attempts to switch bodies with Piccolo, and Bulma receives her body back when Gohan throws her in the way of the technique. Bulma is then blown away from the battlefield and later uses Ginyu to try to find out how the battle is progressing. During the Garlic Jr. arc, Bulma falls under the control of the Black Water Mist, leading her to attack her unaffected friends, being freed of the condition later on. In ''[[Dragon Ball GT]]'', she becomes possessed by [[Baby (Dragon Ball)|Baby]], who takes her as his apparent queen (or second in command), as possessing Vegeta gave him all of his memories and emotions. During this time, she organizes the migration to Planet Vegeta (renamed Planet Tuffle), and creates the {{nihongo|Super Bruits Wave Generator|超ブルーツ波発生装置|Chō Burūtsuha Hassei Sōchi}} that helps Baby become the Saiyan's Golden Great Ape transformation. Later, she helps Vegeta reach Super Saiyan 4 by exposing him to a new Super Bruits Wave Generator, and witnesses [[Omega Shenron]]'s defeat at the hands of Goku.''Dragon Ball GT'' anime, episode 64 Bulma usually appears as a non-playable character in cut scenes for most ''Dragon Ball'' video games, such as ''[[Dragon Ball: Advanced Adventure|Advanced Adventure]]'', ''[[Dragon Ball Z: Budokai|Budokai]]'' and ''[[Dragon Ball Z: Budokai 3|Budokai 3]]''. {{nihongo|'''Madoka Kaname'''|鹿目 まどか|Kaname Madoka|lead=yes}} is the main [[protagonist]] of the 2011 Japanese [[anime]] television series ''[[Puella Magi Madoka Magica]]''. Madoka is a kind and gentle girl who initially lives a normal and happy life, but is suddenly faced with the decision of becoming a [[magical girl]]. She aspires to become a magical girl after witnessing her senior [[Mami Tomoe]] fighting against [[surrealism|surreal]] monsters known as ''witches'' in order to protect people. In ''[[Puella Magi Madoka Magica the Movie: Rebellion]]'', Madoka appears as a magical girl and joins her friends in fighting new monsters known as ''nightmares''. She appears in most ''Puella Magi Madoka Magica'' related-media, including [[manga]], novels and [[video game]]s. Madoka Kaname is voiced by [[Aoi Yūki]] in Japanese, and [[Christine Marie Cabanos]] in English.

In developing the character, writer [[Gen Urobuchi]] imagined the series' protagonist would be a girl with a "cheerful and idealistic" personality, in contrast to his usual writing style. Madoka was designed by [[Ume Aoki]], who used the character Yuno from her manga ''[[Hidamari Sketch]]'' as a base. Although her theme color was intended to be white, it later was changed to pink. Aoki also noted the difficulty of drawing Madoka due to her double ponytail hair.

Madoka has ranked highly in various polls, placing second in the Best Female Category at the 1st [[Newtype Anime Awards]] in 2011, as well ranking seventh in a top 10 anime heroines poll conducted by [[NHK]] in 2013. Her character has been well received by fans and critics, with reviewers praising her character transformation and resonance with the series' other characters, particularly her relationship with [[Homura Akemi]].

==Creation and development==
In the initial planning meeting of the ''[[Puella Magi Madoka Magica]]'' franchise, which began as a 2011 [[anime]] television series, writer [[Gen Urobuchi]] imagined that the heroine of the series would be a girl with a "cheerful and idealistic" personality. Madoka is an unusual character for Urobuchi's writing style, and fits more closely to character designer [[Ume Aoki]]'s worldview. In order to incorporate a "foreign character that did not exist inside [himself]," Urobuchi wrote the initial script as if Yuno, the main character of Aoki's [[manga]] series ''[[Hidamari Sketch]]'', was the [[protagonist]]. During this phase, Urobuchi even intended [[Kana Asumi]] to take on the voice acting role for Madoka. The personality of Madoka was specifically designed as an "Ume Aoki character", while other characters of the cast, such as [[Homura Akemi]] and [[Sayaka Miki]], are more typical for Urobuchi's style.<ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=[[Newtype]]|publisher=[[Kadokawa Shoten]]|title=Gen Urobuchi Interview|date=July 2011|pages=30–31}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=オトナアニメ [Otona Anime] |date=9 May 2011 |publisher={{Interlanguage link|Yosensha|ja|3=洋泉社}} |volume=20 |language=ja |chapter=Sayaka and Madoka}}</ref> Urobuchi said that in the beginning, there was an idea to write the story as "Homura strives to save Madoka", therefore, he created the characteristics of Madoka and Homura as a contrast to each other.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.switch-pub.co.jp/culture/188110002.php#n02|title=【ネ申1oo】003虚淵玄|website=SWITCH-publishing|date=July 7, 2011|access-date=March 29, 2020|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130403031430/http://www.switch-pub.co.jp/culture/188110002.php#n02|archive-date=April 3, 2013}}</ref> Madoka's birthday, October 3, was chosen as it was the file creation date of the series' initial project proposal.<ref>{{cite web|last=Loo|first=Egan|title=Madoka Magica's Urobuchi Tells Why October 3 Is Madoka's Birthday|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interest/2012-10-03/madoka-magica-urobuchi-tells-why-october-3-is-madoka-birthday|publisher=[[Anime News Network]]|access-date=January 7, 2021|date=October 4, 2012}}</ref>

===Design===
[[File:UltimateMadoka.jpg|thumb|right|Ultimate Madoka's design illustrated by Ume Aoki]]
Madoka was designed by [[Ume Aoki]],<ref name="megami">{{cite journal|journal=[[Megami Magazine]]|script-title=ja:新房昭之×虚淵玄×蒼樹うめ×シャフト 1大プロジェクト始動|trans-title=Akiyuki Shinbo × Gen Urobuchi × Ume Aoki × Shaft: The Start of One Large Project|issue=127|publisher=[[Gakken]]|date=October 25, 2010|pages=115|language=Japanese}}</ref> who initially used the protagonist of her manga ''Hidamari Sketch'', Yuno, as a prototype to design Madoka; she created Madoka's design after exaggerating part of its image.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Puella Magi Madoka Magica Production Note|isbn=978-4896106268|publisher=[[Shaft (company)|SHAFT]]|page=135|language=Japanese|edition=Limited}}</ref> Although Madoka's theme color was initially intended to be white as suggested by Urobuchi in the series' draft, Aoki forgot this when designing the character, and changed the main color of Madoka to pink.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Puella Magi Madoka Magica Official Guidebook: You Are Not Alone|page=106|isbn=978-4832240612|publisher=[[Houbunsha]]|language=Japanese}}</ref> Aoki said that in terms of character design, drawing Madoka was more difficult than [[Sayaka Miki]] and [[Kyoko Sakura]], particularly because of the double ponytail design of Madoka's hair, stating that once the size and painting of the ponytail are different, "it looks like a completely different role".<ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=Manga Time Kirara Magica|publisher=[[Houbunsha]]|title=Ume Aoki Interview|volume=3|date=October 10, 2012|pages=8–10|language=Japanese}}</ref> Another difference with other [[magical girl]]s is that in the story, when Madoka transforms into her magical girl outfit, is the result of the appearance of the magical girl in her dream.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Puella Magi Madoka Magica Official Guidebook: You Are Not Alone|isbn=978-4832240612|publisher=[[Houbunsha]]|pages=100–103|language=Japanese}}</ref> For this reason, the dress design especially added ruffles and several decorative elements.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Puella Magi Madoka Magica Official Guidebook: You Are Not Alone|isbn=978-4832240612|publisher=[[Houbunsha]]|pages=46–47|language=Japanese}}</ref> Overall, Aoki incorporated [[fairy tale]] elements and designed a very "cute" magical girl costume. However, Aoki also stated that Madoka's dress is not suitable for fighting.<ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=[[Megami Magazine]]|publisher=[[Gakken]]|title=Interview with Ume Aoki|issue=January 2011|pages=32|language=Japanese}}</ref>

After seeing the character design, the president of the series' animation studio [[Shaft (company)|SHAFT]], [[Mitsutoshi Kubota]], thought that it was a good that the production team got in touch with a new style, but it also brought challenges to the animation production. Recalling this, Aoki did not expect that her style would be adapted directly, although it could bring the feeling of the character Madoka.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Puella Magi Madoka Magica Official Guidebook: You Are Not Alone|page=102|isbn=978-4832240612|publisher=[[Houbunsha]]|language=Japanese}}</ref> In addition, the animation production team also tried to avoid some exaggerated expressions, such as broken clothes, huge sweat beads or emoticons.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Puella Magi Madoka Magica Production Note|isbn=978-4896106268|publisher=[[Shaft (company)|SHAFT]]|page=8|language=Japanese|edition=Limited}}</ref>

Her Ultimate Magical girl form, was also designed by Aoki. She designed her costume based on white theme color and [[cherry blossom]]s, and designed her hair to be longer and her eyes to change from pink to gold, suggesting Madoka's new form of magical girl.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Puella Magi Madoka Magica Official Guidebook: You Are Not Alone|page=43|isbn=978-4832240612|publisher=[[Houbunsha]]|language=Japanese}}</ref> Ultimate Madoka's form has been described as "the ultimate form that has undergone a super evolution by fighting infinite space-time"; according to the ''Puella Magi Madoka Magica The Beginning Story'' guidebook, the form was originally called "Hyper Ultimate Madoka" in the series draft, but was later changed to "Ultimate Madoka".<ref>{{cite book|title=魔法少女まどか☆マギカ Ｔｈｅ Ｂｅｇｉｎｎｉｎｇ Ｓｔｏｒｙ (日本語) 単行本 –|date=December 10, 2011|isbn=978-4041100455|page=164|publisher=[[Kadokawa Shoten]]|language=Japanese}}</ref>

==Appearances==
===In ''Puella Magi Madoka Magica''===
Madoka is a kind and gentle girl who comes from a loving family.<ref name=ep1>{{cite episode|title=As If I Met Her in My Dream...|series=Puella Magi Madoka Magica|network=MBS & TBS|airdate=January 7, 2011|number=1}}</ref> A second-year at middle school, her life changes when she encounters the messenger of magic, [[Kyubey]], who offers to transform her into a magical girl.<ref name=ep1/> She sees herself as a person without special qualities or talents, and after seeing her schoolmate [[Mami Tomoe]] fighting against witches, aspires to become a magical girl like her.<ref name=ep2>{{cite episode|title=That Would Be Truly Wonderful|series=Puella Magi Madoka Magica|network=MBS & TBS|airdate=January 14, 2011|number=2}}</ref> Averse to fighting, she hopes that the magical girls will support each other, sometimes even putting her own life at risk to help them, and is distressed by the infighting they often engage in.<ref>{{cite episode|title=There's No Way I'll Ever Regret It|series=Puella Magi Madoka Magica|network=MBS & TBS|airdate=February 4, 2011|number=5}}</ref> After witnessing Mami's death, she grows uncertain about becoming a magical girl, growing ever more hesitant as the true cost of the role is revealed to her.<ref>{{cite episode|title=Miracles and Magic Are Real|series=Puella Magi Madoka Magica|network=MBS & TBS|airdate=January 28, 2011|number=4}}</ref><ref name=ep8>{{cite episode|title=I Was Stupid, So Stupid|series=Puella Magi Madoka Magica|network=MBS & TBS|airdate=February 25, 2011|number=8}}</ref> Kyubey claims that Madoka has an impossibly large amount of potential for magic, going so far as to claim that she could become the savior of all the magical girls. The reason for this is unclear, since her life so far has been relatively average and free of tragedies.<ref name=ep8/> This is later revealed to be due to her accumulated misfortune, which was caused as a result of her classmate [[Homura Akemi]] repeatedly resetting time, with Madoka's fate getting worse with each timeline, making her magic power grow exponentially with each reset.<ref name=ep11>{{cite episode|title=The Only Thing I Have Left to Guide Me|series=Puella Magi Madoka Magica|network=MBS & TBS|airdate=April 21, 2011|number=11}}</ref>

In previous timelines, Madoka became a magical girl in a pink dress wielding a rose branch bow and arrow.<ref name=ep10>{{cite episode|title=I Won't Rely on Anyone Anymore|series=Puella Magi Madoka Magica|network=MBS & TBS|airdate=March 11, 2011|number=10}}</ref> In the drama CD, "Memories of You", it is revealed that the wish in the first timeline was to save a cat named Amy from death. However, every time, she was either killed or transformed into a witch named Kriemhild Gretchen, the Witch of Salvation, one that became ever more powerful with each time reset, as Madoka's power also increased and if created would, by the end of that same week, consume all life on Earth in order to create a paradise where there is no free will or individuality to cause strife or conflict. In the first timeline, she still possesses a high amount of power, being able to defeat {{nihongo|[[Walpurgis Night|Walpurgisnacht]]|ワルプルギスの夜|Warupurugisu no Yoru}}, though dying in the process.<ref name=ep10/> Subsequently, by the current timeline, she has the potential to be the most powerful magical girl to date.<ref name=ep11/> Towards the end, she learns of this and Homura's efforts to save her.<ref name=ep11/> After seeing the suffering of magical girls throughout history, Madoka decides to make her wish: to prevent all magical girls from the past, present, future and all other timelines, from ever becoming witches. The laws of the universe are rewritten such that at the moment that a soul gem becomes black with anguish, Madoka appears and purifies it before the magical girl passes on. As a result of this wish, she becomes an omnipotent being named {{nihongo|''Ultimate Madoka''|アルティメット・まどか|Arutimetto Madoka}}, that exists for all time, erasing her pre-ascension existence from the world; leaving only Homura – and to some extent her little brother – with the memory of her. Madoka becomes only a concept in the new world, one named the {{nihongo|Law of Cycles|円環の理|Enkan no Kotowari}}. Magical girls absorbed into the Law of Cycles regain knowledge of their lives in previous timelines.<ref name=ep12>{{cite episode|title=My Very Best Friend|series=Puella Magi Madoka Magica|network=MBS & TBS|airdate=April 21, 2011|number=12}}</ref>

At the end of ''Rebellion'', Ultimate Madoka was usurped by Homura and had her human selves split, with her role as a martyr being forced onto the Incubators. Homura places human Madoka in a new universe where she and her friends can live normal lives unaware of their pasts, though Madoka almost regains her memories at the last second and her final conversation with Homura implies that it is only a matter of time before Madoka merges with her self once more and must face her friend in battle.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nerdreactor.com/2012/03/02/puella-magi-madoka-magica-anime-review-magical-girls-have-never-been-so-fun/|publisher=Nerd Reactor|title=Puella Magi Madoka Magica review – Magical Girls have never been so fun|last=Del Castillo|first=Chris|date=March 2, 2012|access-date=February 25, 2016|archive-date=February 13, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220213131953/https://nerdreactor.com/2012/03/02/puella-magi-madoka-magica-anime-review-magical-girls-have-never-been-so-fun/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Madoka will return in ''Puella Magi Madoka Magica The Movie - Walpurgisnacht: Rising''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hodgkins |first=Crystalyn |date=April 25, 2021 |title=Madoka Magica Gets New Anime Film as Sequel to 2013 Rebellion Film |url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2021-04-25/.172103 |access-date=April 25, 2021 |website=[[Anime News Network]] |publisher=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://strangecastnews.com/madoka-magica-movie-announcement-its-not-over-yet/|publisher=Strange Cast News|title=Madoka Magica Movie Announcement: It's Not Over Yet|date=April 25, 2021|access-date=December 16, 2021|archive-date=December 16, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211216161845/https://strangecastnews.com/madoka-magica-movie-announcement-its-not-over-yet/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Critical response===
Madoka's character has been well received by critics. Rachael Verret of ''[[The Mary Sue]]'' praised Madoka's character development for changing from a "naive, noncommittal little girl to someone who recognizes the necessity of relying and trusting in herself, turning into a fully actualized woman taking the power back in a hopeless situation," and referred to her transformation as a "pretty jaw-dropping scene".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.themarysue.com/psychopathy-feminism-and-narrative-agency-in-madoka-magica/|title=Psychopathy, Feminism, and Narrative Agency in Madoka Magica: Kyubey's Story|first=Rachael|last=Verret|publisher=[[The Mary Sue]]|date=June 10, 2015|accessdate=June 10, 2015}}</ref> Theorin Martin from ''[[Anime News Network]]'' listed Madoka making her wish as "Scene of the Year" of 2012, complimenting how her wish "was the culmination of everything that she had learned over the course of the series and everything that she was as a character", calling it "masterstroke".<ref>{{cite news|last=Martin|first=Theorin|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/feature/2013-01-01/|title=Anime in America: The Best (And Most Notable) of 2012|work=[[Anime News Network]]|date=January 1, 2013|accessdate=January 1, 2013}}</ref> Lynzee Loveridge of the same site listed Madoka third in "biggest crybaby heroes" list, noting how Madoka experiences horrible things throughout the story despite being a normal girl, stating that it makes her "more relatable to the audience".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/the-list/2013-04-27|title=7 Biggest Crybaby Heroes|work=[[Anime News Network]]|first=Lynzee|last=Loveridge|date=April 27, 2013|accessdate=April 27, 2013}}</ref> Juliet Kahn of ''[[Looper (website)|Looper]]'' liked how Madoka developed "from a naive young girl into a terrified pawn" and praised the character for realizing her power and for changing the world from despair to a better place, stating that "the momentum this creates is felt on the most visceral level, catapulting the viewer from horror into awe within one episode".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.looper.com/177480/the-best-anime-of-the-past-decade/|title=The best anime of the past decade|work=[[Looper (website)|Looper]]|first=Juliet|last=Kahn|date=December 3, 2019|access-date=May 21, 2020}}</ref> ''[[THEM Anime Reviews]]'' reviewer Jacob Churosh stated that it is easy to view Madoka as a useless character but "there are moments where we see that she is no coward", and "that this kind of desperation is new to her and she knows there is something wrong with her attitude".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.themanime.org/viewreview.php?id=1352|title=''Puella Magi Madoka Magica''|publisher=[[THEM Anime Reviews]]|first=Jacob|last=Churosh|access-date=May 21, 2020}}</ref> James Beckett from ''Anime News Network'' stated that while Madoka may not be the most important character of the series' first episodes, "her deep and complex emotional resonance with every other character" in the series "made her a vital thread in the fabric of its story".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/magia-record-puella-magi-madoka-magica-side-story/episode-11/.157543|title=Magia Record: Puella Magi Madoka Magica Side Story Episode 11|work=[[Anime News Network]]|first=James|last=Beckett|date=March 17, 2019|access-date=May 21, 2020}}</ref> Zac Bertschy from the same site felt that Madoka "does not have that much to do" in first few episodes, and believed that she had played a bigger role in the rest of the story.<ref name=bluray>{{cite news |last=Bertschy |first=Zac |date=April 11, 2012 |title=Puella Magi Madoka Magica Limited Edition Blu-Ray Vol. 2 |work=[[Anime News Network]] |url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/puella-magi-madoka-magica/limited-edition-blu-ray-vol-2 |access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref> Furthermore, he praised her "intense" transformation and characterization for the last episodes, stating "it winds up justifying all the self-doubt the Madoka character goes through in the episodes leading up to this and feels like an even bigger take (and gentle commentary on) the entire idea of a "magical girl" and called her the "very concept of hope itself" that was "immensely emotionally satisfying" to watch.<ref name=bluray />

Madoka's relationship with Homura has also been met with positive critical response. Jacob Hope Chapman from ''Anime News Network'' noted how more powerful became Madoka and Homura's relationship which he also considered one of the film's greatest strengths.<ref>{{cite news |last=Chapman |first=Jacob |date=December 12, 2013 |title=Puella Magi Madoka Magica the Movie Part 3: Rebellion Limited Edition Blu-ray |work=[[Anime News Network]] |url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/puella-magi-madoka-magica-the-movie-part-3/rebellion |access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref> Geoff Berkshire from ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' described Madoka and Homura's friendship as "deep" and "loving".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2013/film/reviews/puella-magi-madoka-magica-the-movie-rebellion-review-1200922803/|title=Film Review: ''Puella Magi Madoka Magica the Movie — Rebellion''|first=Geoff|last=Berkshire|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=December 5, 2013|access-date=August 31, 2020}}</ref> David West of ''[[Neo (magazine)|Neo]]'' said that Urobuchi "takes their friendship and flips it inside-out." West wrote; "Far more complicated than merely turning friends into enemies, Rebellion takes their relationship and stands it in front of a funhouse mirror."<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.neomag.co.uk/art/anime-manga/review/2626/puella-magi-madoka-magica|title=Puella Magi Madoka Magica|first=David|last=West|magazine=[[Neo (magazine)|Neo]]|date=November 22, 2015|access-date=August 31, 2020|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170906224839/http://www.neomag.co.uk/art/anime-manga/review/2626/puella-magi-madoka-magica|archive-date=September 6, 2017}}</ref> Writing for ''A Cycle, Not a Phase: Love Between Magical Girls Amidst the Trauma of Puella Magi Madoka Magica'', Kevin Cooley argues that Homura's powers are not merely a "metaphor for love between magical girls," but "literally are the love between magical girls" and that Madoka's actions create a world "where love between women can prosper free from Kyubey's policing."<ref>{{Cite journal|first=Kevin|last=Cooley|date=2020|title=A Cycle, Not a Phase: Love Between Magical Girls Amidst the Trauma of Puella Magi Madoka Magica|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/10.5749/mech.13.1.0024|journal=Mechademia: Second Arc|volume=13|issue=1|pages=33|doi=10.5749/mech.13.1.0024|jstor=10.5749/mech.13.1.0024|s2cid=226967395|via=|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Kory Cerjak from ''The Fandom Post'' praised the work of [[Christine Marie Cabanos]], Madoka's [[Voice acting in Japan|voice actress]], noting that while it felt like "an adult playing a junior high school student" in the series' beginning, by the movies, it had become more appealing and suitable.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fandompost.com/2014/09/10/puella-magi-madoka-magica-the-movie-parts-1-2-limited-edition-blu-ray-anime-review-2/|title= Puella Magi Madoka Magica The Movie Parts 1–2 Limited Edition Blu-ray Anime Review |first=Kory|last=Cerjak|work= The Fandom Post |date= September 10, 2014 |access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref>

===Analysis===
Japanese critic [[Kenichi Yamakawa]] noted the contrasts between Madoka and Homura, stating Madoka represents "people's justice" while Homura represents "human love".<ref>{{Cite book|title=A Cage Named Maturity On Puella Magi Madoka Magica|author=[[Kenichi Yamakawa]]|date=August 10, 2011|publisher=[[Kinema Junpo]]|isbn=978-4873763743 |language=Japanese}}</ref> [[Sociologist]] [[Shinji Miyadai]] noted that Madoka is a heroine who moves forward and never looks back. He stated that the story is about Madoka's growth; an average girl that realizes the bonds between those surrounding her and the people supporting her, which eventually made her accept her role and fulfill her duty in saving magical girls from their cruel fate.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Miyadai |first=Shinji |date=July 19, 2011 |title=大人気アニメ『まどか☆マギカ』の正体 |trans-title=Identity of the popular anime “Madoka Magica" |magazine=SPA! |publisher=Nikkan SPA! |page=56 |language=Japanese |volume=10}}</ref> Additionally, critic Tetsuya Miyazaki believes that ''Puella Magi Madoka Magica'' refers to the causal view of [[Buddhism]] and adopts the world setting of "hope is born from despair". Miyazaki believes that the theme of the story is about Madoka growing up and saves all magical girls, and referred to her as an ordinary girl that follows the steps of [[Bodhisattva]] and [[Tathagata]]. Miyazaki further commented on Madoka creating a new world, to which he described as the pure land and said Madoka herself becomes omnipresent in this universe by turning into a person that transcends time and laws. Furthermore, Miyazaki also found Madoka realizing her destiny and making an independent choice in the final episode as magnificent.<ref name="SPA">{{Cite magazine |last=Miyazaki |first=Tetsuya |date=19 July 2011 |title=大人気アニメ『まどか☆マギカ』の正体 |trans-title=Identity of the popular anime “Madoka Magica" |magazine=SPA! |publisher=Nikkan SPA! |page=71 |language=Japanese |volume=10}}</ref>

Critic Ryōta Fujitsu believes that the series should be analyzed from the context of beautiful girl games and sci-fi literature, and described the story as "understanding mother's lifestyle and taking it as a decision in life", and the coming of age story of Madoka. Fujitsu also believes that in episode 11, Madoka's determination to confront her mother until her mother watched Madoka leave was the most exciting part of the plot of the series.<ref>{{Cite book|first=Ryota|last=Fujitsu|date=May 5, 2011|title=茶話 アニメ 魔法少女の成長物語|publisher=[[Asahi Shimbun]]|page=}}</ref> According to comments in SPA magazine, the deep friendship and bond of Madoka and Homura caused a miracle to happen, with Madoka developing into a realized person due to learning about Homura's sufferings and the support of her mother Junko.<ref name="SPA"/>

Writing for ''The Very Soil: An Unauthorized Critical Study of Puella Magi Madoka Magica'', Jed A. Blue said that Madoka resembles the Bodhisattva [[Guanyin]], a figure from Buddhist mythology, as Madoka takes the suffering of all magical girls and guides them to her heaven and said that Madoka "becomes a force of nature, an incarnation of hope, dissolving her consciousness, and attaining [[Nirvana (Buddhism)|nirvana]]".<ref>{{Cite book|title=The Very Soil: An Unauthorized Critical Study of ''Puella Magi Madoka Magica''|first=Jed A.|last=Blue|date=March 2015|pages=86–87|publisher=Distributed via Smashwords. |isbn=978-1-3119-5733-7 }}</ref> Similarly, Madoka has also been compared to [[Goethe]]'s character Gretchen from ''[[Faust (Goethe)|Faust]]'', Blue said: "Madoka's wish to guide magical girls away from being witches parallels Gretchen's wish to guide Faust into Heaven. Madoka also takes on a role as a savior and protector, similar to that taken in Faust by the Marian, divine principle of the [[eternal feminine]], with which Gretchen is associated".<ref>{{Cite book|title=The Very Soil: An Unauthorized Critical Study of ''Puella Magi Madoka Magica''|first=Jed A.|last=Blue|date=March 2015|page=85|publisher=Distributed via Smashwords. |isbn=978-1-3119-5733-7 }}</ref> Noelle Ogawa of [[Crunchyroll]] called her a "somewhat unconventional main character", and that she "never becomes the superpowered hero that fights monsters and villains. She does not even start out with the desire to change the world, she grows into the role of being the world's savior".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.crunchyroll.com/anime-feature/2020/10/06/feature-madoka-kaname-from-wallflower-to-goddess|title=FEATURE: Madoka Kaname, From Wallflower to Goddess|first=Noelle|last=Ogawa|publisher=[[Crunchyroll]]|date=October 6, 2020|accessdate=October 6, 2020}}</ref>
